title: Personal Checking: Per-Tier Account Limits and Age-Based Conversion Targets
content:
Personal Checking fixes, tier by tier, how many open accounts of that one tier a single customer may hold as primary owner, and whether an account of the tier moves automatically into another tier once its owner reaches a stated age.

## Parameters

- **Accounts of this tier per customer** — the ceiling on open accounts of the particular tier that one customer may hold as primary owner (a whole number).
- **Conversion age** — the age, in whole years, at which an account of the tier is moved automatically into another tier at a statement cycle close; "not applicable" where the tier has no such move.
- **Conversion target** — the official name of the tier the account becomes at the conversion age; "not applicable" where no automatic move exists.

## Table

| Tier | Accounts of this tier per customer | Conversion age | Conversion target |
|---|---|---|---|
| Access Checking | 1 | not applicable | not applicable |
| Student Checking | 1 | 25 | Everyday Checking |
| Everyday Checking | 4 | not applicable | not applicable |
| Interest Checking | 4 | not applicable | not applicable |
| Premier Checking | 2 | not applicable | not applicable |
| Private Client Checking | 2 | not applicable | not applicable |

## Points of judgement

- Student Checking is the one tier with an automatic age-based move; its accounts become Everyday Checking when the owner reaches 25.
- A per-tier ceiling of 1 means a customer who already holds one open Access Checking account, or one open Student Checking account, holds the most that tier allows.
- A hypothetical customer holding two open Premier Checking accounts has reached that tier's ceiling of 2; the Premier figure says nothing about Everyday Checking, whose own ceiling is 4.
